Cache per-stage reco-energy spectra and the irreducible-muDIF arrays.

Derived from tail_final_reco.py (identical joins, weights, window); plots are drawn

Thesis-style tail cutflows on the MAIN model's reconstructed quantities.

Same chains, weights, annotations, and page-format layouts as the truth-quantity cutflows of
tail_thesis_figures.py, with three swaps per event: the reconstructed acceptance decision for
the truth flag, the reconstructed positron energy plus the reconstructed dead-material
estimate for the true deposit, and the consensus positron time for the true time. The prompt
window is anchored data-driven at the reconstructed pie onset (+2 to +32 ns), so the time
frame convention of each generation cannot shift the cut.

Inputs (all positional joins, verified per piece by float32 equality of the tail predictions'
deposited_energy against the main summaries' truth_live_E):
  pie    : norad_eval2_drop tail predictions x purity_eval/nodrop_ep12_pie main summaries
  michel : michel_eval_inwin_drop tail predictions x purity_eval/nodrop_ep12_michel_inwin
           main summaries (RMD removed via truth_event_type bit 0x200, per analysis policy)
  piDIF  : eval10 eval-mode tail predictions x purity_eval/tail_osl pidif summaries

Outputs: figures/AI/tail_cutflow_michel_reco_ep19.png, tail_cutflow_pidif_reco_ep19.png, and the
'mudar_cutflow_reco' / 'pidif_cutflow_reco' blocks in figures/AI/tail_stats.json.

modules.historical_module_docstring:
Thesis-style tail-reveal figures for the AI chapter, generated from the settled eval parquets.

Ports the SETTLED analysis logic verbatim from:
  cutflow_settled.py   (muDAR 5-panel chain, gen-weighted michel, kPienu+kMudif removed)
  cutflow_pidif.py     (piDIF 4-panel chain, absolute [6,36] ns window on norad/eval10 samples)
  dif_mudif_corrected.py (muDIF suppression spectrum + delta-ray-corrected tail-fraction sweep)
  mudif_tradeoff.py    (bias vs contamination working-point curve, pie5M Ecorr, 20:1 norm)
  mudif_surv_analysis.py (survivor muon E-deposition / decay-KE, suppression vs angle)
and renders in the thesis figure style (figures/ml_pedagogy/figstyle.py conventions).
Outputs PNGs to thesis_ref/figures/AI/ and a stats JSON alongside.

modules.coverage: Render the three reconstructed background cutflows from cached spectra.
modules.historical_module_docstring:
The tail-reveal cutflows: one panel per background, drawn from the cached spectra.

The background spectrum is drawn at every stage of its chain in successively lighter
shades, so the reader watches it melt away from under the \pie spectrum, whose low-energy
tail stays visible because the vertical range is set from the data.  Legends sit above the
axes and quote each stage as the surviving fraction of the accepted sample.

modules.coverage: Render before/after spectra and the historical combined annotation.
modules.historical_module_docstring:
FIGURE -- the whole tail measurement in two panels: every channel before and after.

Left: \pie and the three backgrounds at acceptance, at their physical rates per stopped
pion.  Right: the same four after the complete selection chain.  The Michel and piDIF
spectra vanish, the muDIF residue survives at the loose working point, and the \pie
low-energy tail stands revealed below the 56 MeV line.

modules.coverage: Render angular suppression and signal-tail bias from central prediction columns.
modules.historical_module_docstring:
FIGURE 10 -- why an aggressive muDIF veto biases the tail.

Three stacked panels against the true positron polar angle, all from the train-mode
central cache (58 MB, safe outside SLURM):

  (a) muDIF suppression of a tight in-flight-muon veto;
  (b) the fraction of accepted pie events that veto removes;
  (c) the pie tail fraction, the quantity the selection must not sculpt.

The point of the figure is the alignment of (b) and (c): the veto removes pie
preferentially at the angles where the tail fraction is largest, which is how an
energy-blind topological cut acquires an energy bias.

modules.coverage: Render the retuned muon-DIF contamination versus bias scan.
modules.historical_module_docstring:
FIGURE 11 -- the muDIF veto trade-off: contamination against induced tail bias.

One curve on the two axes the requirement is written in. Both quantities are plotted so that
"worse" runs the same way, the bias as a magnitude on a logarithmic axis, so the desirable
corner is the empty bottom left and the failure to reach it is geometry rather than assertion.
The veto threshold rides on the marker colour, which keeps the scan knob visible without a
single label on the plane. No fit is drawn: the points bend away from a power law at the loose
end, and a line through them would misstate the data exactly where the reader looks.

modules.coverage: Render accepted and tight-veto muon-DIF deposit/decay-energy densities.
modules.historical_module_docstring:
FIGURE 12 -- the irreducible muDIF population, as two densities on one scale.

The plane is (energy the muon deposited in the ATAR) against (its kinetic energy at the
moment of decay).  Left: all accepted muDIF events.  Right: the survivors of the complete
selection chain with the veto at its tightest.  Each panel is normalized to its own sample,
so the two densities are directly comparable: the accepted population runs down the
energy-conservation band, while the survivors abandon it for the top-left corner, full
birth energy and less than a single MIP deposit.

modules.coverage: Build the historical Michel source-overlap masks and report the three-way cutflow.
modules.historical_module_docstring:
Audit and fix the michel_inwin training leak.

combine_partition_michel2.py's sorted-glob prefix swept all 550 shards of generation job
1595422 into the michel pools, and groups t000-t044 of that job are the tail-reveal model's
TRAINING michel groups (tail10_chain.sbatch / mix_shard_tail.py). Every michel_inwin piece
therefore carries ~12.7% trigger decays the tail model trained on.

This job:
  1. builds the exact truth-key set of the leaked decays (495 source shards, 4 float32 keys);
  2. flags every michel_inwin event whose trigger decay is in that set (mask parquet/piece);
  3. re-derives the reco-axis muDAR chain (tail_final_reco cuts) on ALL / CLEAN / LEAKED
     subsets, so the memorization question is answered by direct comparison;
  4. recounts the non-time residue on the clean subset and reports whether the displayed
     fig9a event is leaked.

SLURM only.
